newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey to stay in Iraq until job done - minister.
newsitem.headline: Turkey to stay in Iraq until job done - minister.

text.p: Turkey's military incursion into northern Iraq, in its seventh day on Tuesday, will continue until the aim of hunting down separatists Kurdish guerrillas has been achieved, the Turkish defence minister said.

"The operation will continue until results are achieved," Defence Minister Turhan Tayan said in remarks broadcast on Turkish television late on Monday. Turkey has said the army operation is aimed at preventing Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) rebels from using Iraq as a base to launch raids into Turkey.
"We will continue the struggle against the PKK terror group, which troubles Turkey, oppresses the region's people and seeks regional domination," Tayan said.

Thousands of Turkish troops, aided by an Iraq Kurdish militia, have been pursuing PKK guerrillas since early last Wednesday. Turkey says 1,142 PKK members have been killed for the loss of just over dozen Turkish troops.
Sources close to the rebels say the PKK death toll has been exaggerated and that the number of soldiers killed is higher.

An Iraqi opposition group said on Monday the Turkey's Iraqi Kurdish allies, the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP), had driven the PKK out of a key northern city in a bitter settling of scores at the weekend.
A spokesman for the Iraqi National Congress told Reuters the KDP had overrun all six PKK offices in Arbil and executed prisoners.

"The battles in Arbil resulted in 53 KDP (fighters) killed," the spokesman said. "Among the PKK and allied parties, there was a total of 58 dead, 28 of whom were killed after capture," the spokesman, based in London, said.
Northern Iraq has been out of President Saddam Hussein's control since the Kurds broke from Baghdad under Western military protection after the Gulf War in 1991.

Turkey's NATO allies have urged it to tread carefully in northern Iraq and to end the incursion soon. Ankara was criticised abroad for heavy-handedness with the local population in a similar cross-border drive two years ago.
More than 23,000 people have been killed in the PKK's 12-year-old armed struggle with Turkey for self-rule in the southeast of the country.
